questions.question: Which of the following part of the Himalayas located between Kali and Teesta rivers?

• Nepal Himalayas, **east-central section** and highest part of the Himalayan mountain ranges in south-central Asia
 
• **It extending some 500 miles (800 km) from the Kali River east to the Tista River.**
 
• The Great Himalaya range attains maximum height in this portion.
 
• Some of the **world-famous peaks Mt. Everest, Kanchenjunga,** Makalu, Annapurna, Gosainthan, and Dhaulagiri are located here.
 
• The Lesser Himalaya is known as Mahabharat Lekh in this region.
 
• The range is **crossed by rivers like Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi**, etc.
 
• In between the Great and the Lesser Himalayas, there are Kathmandu and Pokhra lacustrine valleys (previously, they were lakes).
 
• The Shiwalik range comes very close to the lesser Himalaya towards the east and is almost non-existent beyond Narayani (Gandak)

questions.question: Which type of spherical mirror is used by dentists to see a large image of the teeth of patients?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concave mirror**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• A **Concave mirror** is the type of spherical mirror used by **dentists** to see a **large (magnified) image** of a patient's teeth.

• The core logic lies in the image formation properties of a concave mirror: when an object is placed very close to the mirror (between the **pole** and the **principal focus**), the resulting image is **virtual**, **erect**, and **magnified**.

• **Plane mirrors** are incorrect because they produce an image that is the **same size** as the object, providing no magnification for detailed dental work.

• **Convex mirrors** are incorrect because they always produce a **diminished** (smaller) image, which would make it harder for a dentist to see details.

• **Bifocal mirrors** is not a standard term in optics; **bifocal lenses** are used in spectacles to correct vision, not for magnification in dental tools.

**Additional Information__**

• **Concave mirrors** are also widely used in **shaving mirrors** and **makeup mirrors** to provide a clear, enlarged view of the face.

• They are used in **torches**, **searchlights**, and **vehicle headlights** to produce a powerful parallel beam of light when the light source is placed at the focus.

• **Convex mirrors** are commonly used as **rear-view mirrors** in vehicles because they give a **wider field of view**, allowing drivers to see a large area of traffic behind them.

• A **spherical mirror** whose reflecting surface is curved inwards (towards the center of the sphere) is a **concave mirror**, while one curved outwards is a **convex mirror**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Vice President of India is INCORRECT?

options.text: Members of State legislatures do not take part in his elections.

The Vice President is elected for five years.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The Vice-President holds office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters his office. ***Hence statement 3 is correct.***
 
• However, he can resign from his office at any time by addressing the **resignation letter to the President.**
 
• He can also be removed from office before the completion of his term.
 
• A formal impeachment is not required for his removal.
 
• He can be removed by a **resolution passed by a majority **of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.*** ******Hence statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• This means that this resolution should be passed in the Rajya Sabha by an effective majority and in the Lok Sabha by a simple majority.
 
• It must be noted here that the effective majority in India is only a type of special majority and not a separate one.
 
• Further, this resolution can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha and not in the Lok Sabha.
 
• But, no such resolution can be moved unless at least 14 days advance notice has been given.
 
• Notably, no ground has been mentioned in the Constitution for his removal.
 
• The Vice-President can hold office beyond his term of five years until his successor assumes charge.
 
• Members of the State legislature do not take part in his elections. *Hence statement 1 is correct.*
 
• He is also eligible for re-election to that office.
 
• He may be elected for any number of terms.

• ARTICLE 64: The Vice-President shall be ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States and shall not hold any other office of profit. *Hence statement 2 is correct.*
 
• ARTICLE 65: The Vice-President shall act as President in the event of the occurrence of any vacancy in the office of the President by reason of this death, resignation or removal, or otherwise.

• **__Urease__**: Requires **__Nickel (Ni²⁺)__** as its cofactor, not **__Copper (Cu²⁺)__**.

questions.question:
With reference to the Vijayanagara Empire, consider the following statements.

1. The Vijayanagara Empire was od founded by Harihara I and Bukka I.

2. Krishnadevaraya, the greatest ruler of the Tuluva dynasty, authored 'Amuktamalyada' in Telugu.al

3. The city of Hampi, the capital of Vijayanagara, was sacked after the Battle of Talikota.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2 - All three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Vijayanagara Empire** was founded by **Harihara I** and **Bukka I** in the year **1336 CE**. They were brothers and served under the Kakatiya dynasty before establishing Vijayanagara. *Hence, Statement 1 is correct.*
 
• **Krishnadevaraya**, the most celebrated ruler of the Tuluva dynasty in Vijayanagara, authored the literary masterpiece **‘Amuktamalyada’** in **Telugu**. This work is considered one of the finest examples of Telugu literature and provides insights into governance and dharma. *Hence, Statement 2 is correct.*
 
• The city of **Hampi**, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, faced destruction after the **Battle of Talikota** in **1565 CE**. The battle was fought between the Vijayanagara Empire and the combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates, resulting in the defeat of Vijayanagara and the subsequent sacking of Hampi. *Hence, Statement 3 is correct.*
 
• All three statements provided in the question align with historical evidence and are correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Harihara I and Bukka I:**

 
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire was established in **1336 CE** by Harihara I and Bukka I, who were originally feudatories under the Kakatiya and Kampili kingdoms.
 
• They founded the empire to protect South India from the invasions of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• The empire served as a beacon of Hindu culture, art, and architecture during its time.
 
 
 
• **Krishnadevaraya:**
 
 
• He ruled Vijayanagara from **1509 to 1529 CE** and is considered one of the greatest rulers of the empire.
 
• Krishnadevaraya was a patron of literature, art, and architecture. His reign saw the construction of several iconic temples, including the **Vitthala Temple** at Hampi.
 
• ‘Amuktamalyada’ is a treatise on statecraft, written in Telugu, focusing on governance principles and the welfare of citizens.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Talikota:**
 
 
• The Battle of Talikota occurred in **1565 CE** between Vijayanagara and the combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates—Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmednagar, and Bidar.
 
• The defeat of Vijayanagara marked the decline of the empire and led to the destruction of Hampi, which was looted and razed.
 
• Hampi, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site, stands as a testament to the architectural and cultural achievements of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
 
 
• **Key Contributions of the Vijayanagara Empire:**
 
 
• The empire played a significant role in the preservation of Hindu culture and traditions during its rule.
 
• Architectural wonders like the **Virupaksha Temple**, **Lotus Mahal**, and the **Stone Chariot** at Hampi showcase the advancements in art and architecture.
 
• The empire facilitated trade and commerce, connecting South India with international markets.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hampi:**

 
 
• Hampi was the capital city of Vijayanagara and a major center for religion, trade, and culture.
 
• It features stunning examples of Dravidian architecture, mixed with Indo-Islamic influences.
 
• Today, Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, attracting tourists and historians worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Literature and Art:**
 
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire was known for its patronage of literature in languages like Telugu, Kannada, Tamil, and Sanskrit.
 
• Poets like Allasani Peddana and Tenali Ramakrishna flourished during Krishnadevaraya’s reign.
 
 
 
• **End of the Empire:**
 
 
• The destruction of Hampi after the Battle of Talikota marked the decline of Vijayanagara, but its cultural and architectural legacy continues to inspire.

questions.question: "Eutrophication" in aquatic ecosystems like Kerala's backwaters is primarily driven by an excess of which nutrients?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitrogen and Phosphorus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eutrophication** is a process where a body of water becomes overly enriched with **minerals** and **nutrients** that induce excessive growth of **algae**.
 
• This phenomenon is primarily driven by the accumulation of **Nitrogen** and **Phosphorus** in the aquatic ecosystem. These nutrients act as **fertilizers** for aquatic plants and microscopic organisms. ***Hence, the statement regarding Nitrogen and Phosphorus is correct.***
 
• The presence of these nutrients leads to **Algal Blooms**, which create a dense layer on the water surface, preventing **sunlight** from penetrating deeper layers of the water body.
 
• As the **algae** die, **microorganisms** like bacteria decompose them, a process that consumes large quantities of **Dissolved Oxygen (DO)**. This leads to a state of **hypoxia**, where oxygen levels are too low to support fish and other aquatic life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sources of Nutrients:** In **India**, particularly in **Kerala's backwaters**, the high concentration of **Nitrogen** and **Phosphorus** is attributed to **agricultural runoff** from the **Kuttanad** region, where **chemical fertilizers** are heavily used in **paddy cultivation**.
 
• **Types of Eutrophication:** 
 
 
• **Natural Eutrophication:** A slow, **geological process** where nutrients accumulate over **centuries** as a lake ages.
 
• **Cultural Eutrophication:** A rapid, **human-induced** process caused by **urbanization**, **industrial waste**, and **domestic sewage**.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Kerala:** The **Vembanad Lake**, a designated **Ramsar Site** in **Kerala**, has suffered significantly from **eutrophication**, leading to the proliferation of **water hyacinths** and a decline in traditional **shrimp** and **fish** farming.
 
• **Consequences:** Beyond **hypoxia**, eutrophication can lead to the production of **toxins** by certain algae (cyanobacteria), which can contaminate **drinking water** and harm **public health**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD):** This is a crucial **numerical value** used to measure **water pollution**. During **eutrophication**, the **BOD** increases significantly because more **oxygen** is needed by **aerobic bacteria** to break down the excess organic matter.
 
• **Limiting Nutrients:** In most **freshwater** ecosystems, **Phosphorus** is the primary **limiting nutrient**, meaning its addition has the most immediate impact on **algal growth**. In **marine** or **brackish** waters, **Nitrogen** often plays this role.
 
• **Regulatory Framework:** The **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** in **India** monitors nutrient levels under the **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974**, to mitigate the degradation of sensitive **aquatic ecosystems**.
 
• **Prevention:** Methods to control **eutrophication** include the **diversion of sewage**, reducing the use of **phosphate-based detergents**, and creating **riparian buffer zones** to filter **agricultural runoff** before it reaches the water.
</ul

questions.question: Geeta runs 5/2 times as fast as Babita. In a race, if Geeta gives a lead of 40 m to Babita, find the distance from the starting point where both of them will meet (correct up to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of speeds (Geeta : Babita) = 5 : 2

Since time is constant, Distance ratio = Speed ratio = 5 : 2

Difference in distance (Lead) = 5 − 2 = 3 units

3 units → 40 m

Distance from start (Geeta's total distance) = 5 units = (40 ÷ 3) × 5 = 200 ÷ 3 ≈ 66.67 m

**∴ The correct answer is 66.67 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Geeta = 5/2 × Speed of Babita

Lead given to Babita = 40 m

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8e111aa4b516ba1a065e38b23005ef18c6e237fc517c85e3d2df0f10667dac5b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the speed of Babita be 2x and the speed of Geeta be 5x.

⇒ Let the meeting point be at a distance D from the starting point.

⇒ Since they meet at the same time:

⇒ Time taken by Geeta = Time taken by Babita

⇒ D ÷ 5x = (D − 40) ÷ 2x

⇒ D ÷ 5 = (D − 40) ÷ 2

⇒ 2D = 5 × (D − 40)

⇒ 2D = 5D − 200

⇒ 3D = 200

⇒ D = 200 ÷ 3 = 66.666...

⇒ D ≈ 66.67 m

**∴ The correct answer is 66.67 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Races

When two people move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = V₁ − V₂.

Distance-Speed Relationship

If time is constant, distance is directly proportional to speed (D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂). If distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

Concept of Lead

A "lead of x meters" means the slower runner starts x meters ahead of the faster runner. To meet, the faster runner must cover this extra distance using their relative speed.</p

questions.question: If the area of a sector is 58.5 cm², then find its perimeter if the radius of the circle is 6.5 cm.
questions.solution:

Arc Length (l) = (2 × Area) ÷ Radius

l = (2 × 58.5) ÷ 6.5 = 117 ÷ 6.5 = 18 cm

Perimeter of Sector = l + 2r

Perimeter = 18 + 2 × 6.5 = 18 + 13 = 31 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 31 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Area of sector = 58.5 cm², Radius (r) = 6.5 cm.

Formula Used: Area = (1/2) × r × l and Perimeter = l + 2r

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6419793b8eb1411e27ba56eb7153f206aa62af962d96b71509cb8d5e3fe4a8e2.png] 

⇒ Area = (1/2) × r × l

⇒ 58.5 = (1/2) × 6.5 × l

⇒ l = (58.5 × 2) ÷ 6.5

⇒ l = 117 ÷ 6.5 = 18 cm

⇒ Perimeter = l + 2r

⇒ Perimeter = 18 + 2 × 6.5

⇒ Perimeter = 18 + 13 = 31 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 31 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Sector (using angle)

Area = (θ/360°) × πr², where θ is the central angle in degrees.

Length of Arc

Arc length (l) = (θ/360°) × 2πr, representing the curved boundary of the sector.

Relation between Area and Arc Length

Area = (Arc length × Radius) ÷ 2. This is useful when the angle θ is unknown.

Perimeter of Sector

Perimeter = Length of Arc + 2 × Radius. It includes both the curved boundary and the two straight radii.</p

questions.question: 10 women take 16 days to complete a work which can be completed by 6 men in 8 days. 12 men started working and after 2 days 6 men left, and 5 women joined them. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency Ratio (W:M) ⇒ 10W × 16 : 6M × 8 ⇒ 160 : 48 ⇒ 10 : 3 (W=3, M=10).

Total Work = 10 × 3 × 16 = 480 units.

Work done by 12 men in 2 days = 12 × 10 × 2 = 240 units.

Remaining Work = 480 − 240 = 240 units.

New Efficiency (6M + 5W) = (6 × 10) + (5 × 3) = 75 units/day.

Total time = 2 + (240 ÷ 75) = 2 + 16/5 = 26/5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 26/5 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Work completed by 10 women in 16 days.

Work completed by 6 men in 8 days.

Initial workforce: 12 men for 2 days.

New workforce: 6 men (12 − 6) and 5 women.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Number of persons × Efficiency × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d62c6411fc840e37698d2eae39a4181045d373599a66e4f2f0c660b5f353d770.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 10 Women × 16 days = 6 Men × 8 days

⇒ 160W = 48M ⇒ 10W = 3M ⇒ M/W = 10/3

⇒ Efficiency of 1 Man (M) = 10 units, 1 Woman (W) = 3 units

⇒ Total Work = 48 × 10 = 480 units

⇒ Work done in first 2 days = 12M × 2 = 12 × 10 × 2 = 240 units

⇒ Remaining Work = 480 − 240 = 240 units

⇒ Efficiency of new group (6M + 5W) = 6(10) + 5(3) = 60 + 15 = 75 units/day

⇒ Time for remaining work = 240 ÷ 75 = 16/5 days

⇒ Total time taken = 2 + 16/5 = 26/5 days

**∴ The correct answer is 26/5 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Work-Efficiency Relationship

Total work is the product of number of workers, their efficiency, and the time taken (Work = M × E × D). For the same work, (M₁D₁E₁) = (M₂D₂E₂).

Combined Efficiency

When different types of workers (men, women, children) work together, their net efficiency is the sum of their individual efficiencies multiplied by their respective counts.

Fractional Days

If work is not finished in a whole number of days, the time is expressed as (Total Work Done) / (Work done per day), often leading to improper fractions like 26/5.</p

questions.question: The value of simple interest and compound interest on a certain principal at a certain rate after two years is Rs. 2400 and Rs. 2544 respectively. Find the value of the principal.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simple interest for 1 year = 2400 ÷ 2 = Rs. 1200

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = 2544 − 2400 = Rs. 144

This difference is the interest generated on the first year's SI.

Rate (R) = (144 ÷ 1200) × 100 = 12%

Principal = (1200 × 100) ÷ 12 = 10000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 10000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = Rs. 2400

Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = Rs. 2544

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

For 2 years, Difference (CI − SI) = P × (R ÷ 100)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a46e9b13b7e0fcbe2b9b675e196124d1f54ce9149b98c64f832b5d813b9e7dd4.png]

⇒ 2400 = (P × R × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ P × R = 120000 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = P × (R ÷ 100)²

⇒ 2544 − 2400 = P × (R² ÷ 10000)

⇒ 144 = (P × R × R) ÷ 10000

⇒ Substitute the value of P × R from Equation 1:

⇒ 144 = (120000 × R) ÷ 10000

⇒ 144 = 12 × R

⇒ R = 12%

⇒ Substitute R = 12 in Equation 1:

⇒ P × 12 = 120000

⇒ P = 10000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 10000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CI vs SI for 2 years

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for exactly two years is calculated using the formula: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)².

CI vs SI for 3 years

For three years, the difference accounts for additional compounding: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)² × (300 + R) ÷ 100.

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

For a 2-year period at a rate of R%, the effective compound interest rate can directly be found as: Effective Rate = 2R + (R² ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: The HCF and the LCM of two numbers are 44 and 264, respectively. If one of the numbers is 3 over 2 times of the other, what is the smaller number?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of the two numbers = 1 : 3/2 = 2 : 3.

Let the common ratio factor be k. Then the numbers are 2k and 3k.

Product of numbers = HCF × LCM ⇒ (2k) × (3k) = 44 × 264.

6k² = 44 × 264 ⇒ k² = 44 × 44 = 1936.

k = √1936 = 44.

Smaller number = 2k = 2 × 44 = 88.

**∴ The correct answer is 88.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

HCF of two numbers = 44

LCM of two numbers = 264

One number (N₁) = 3/2 × Other number (N₂)

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/94d935051c4f490751a2714da874f2983a02ad8d20ad553e1c6ac9d12359970f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the smaller number be x. Then the larger number is (3/2)x.

⇒ x × (3/2)x = 44 × 264

⇒ (3/2)x² = 11616

⇒ x² = (11616 × 2) ÷ 3

⇒ x² = 3872 × 2 = 7744

⇒ x = √7744

⇒ x = 88

The numbers are 88 and (3/2) × 88 = 132.

**∴ The correct answer is 88.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Relation

For any two positive integers a and b, Product (a × b) = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

HCF and Co-primes

If the HCF of two numbers is H, the numbers can be represented as Hx and Hy, where x and y are co-prime integers.

LCM in terms of HCF

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) is always divisible by the Highest Common Factor (HCF). LCM = HCF × x × y.</p

questions.question: If a² + b² + c² = ab + bc + ac, then find the value of a³ + b³ + c³.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For real numbers, the condition a² + b² + c² = ab + bc + ac is satisfied only when a = b = c.

Let a = b = c = 1. Then, 1² + 1² + 1² = 1×1 + 1×1 + 1×1 ⇒ 3 = 3.

Substitute these values into the required expression: a³ + b³ + c³ = 1³ + 1³ + 1³ = 3.

Among the options, 3abc = 3 × 1 × 1 × 1 = 3, which matches the result.

**∴ The correct answer is 3abc.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: a² + b² + c² = ab + bc + ac

Formula Used: a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ac)

⇒ a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ac = 0

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c) × (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ac)

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c) × 0

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 0

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc

**∴ The correct answer is 3abc.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cubic Algebra Identity

The general expansion is a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ac).

Special Conditional Case

If a + b + c = 0, then the entire product on the right side becomes zero, resulting in a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

Equality Condition for Squares

The expression a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ac can be rewritten as 1/2[(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²]. For real numbers, this is 0 only when a = b = c.</p

questions.question: A student scored 20% less and another student scored 25% more than the average marks of the class. What is the ratio of the 1st student to the average score of the student to the another student?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let the average marks of the class be 100 units.

Score of 1st student = 100 − 20 = 80 units.

Score of 2nd student = 100 + 25 = 125 units.

Required Ratio = 80 : 100 : 125.

Simplifying by dividing each part by 5: 16 : 20 : 25.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 : 20 : 25.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Score of 1st student = 20% less than Average.

Score of 2nd student = 25% more than Average.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the average marks of the class be x.

⇒ Marks of 1st student = x − (20/100) × x = x − 0.2x = 0.8x.

⇒ Marks of 2nd student = x + (25/100) × x = x + 0.25x = 1.25x.

⇒ Required Ratio = (Score of 1st student) : (Average Marks) : (Score of 2nd student)

⇒ Required Ratio = 0.8x : x : 1.25x

⇒ Required Ratio = 0.8 : 1 : 1.25

⇒ To remove decimals, multiply by 100: 80 : 100 : 125.

⇒ Required Ratio = 16 : 20 : 25.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 : 20 : 25.**
